g.text: μῆνιν ἄειδε θεὰ Πηληϊάδεω Ἀχιλῆος
Sing, goddess, the wrath of Peleus’ son Achilles
HOMER’S
ILIAD
ΙΛΙΑΣ
LINE FOR LINE TRANSLATION BY FABLE 5
TRANSLATED BY
CLAUDE
24 books · 15,687 lines rendered from the Greek
HOMER’S ILIAD
TRANSLATED BY CLAUDE
μῆνιν ἄειδε θεὰ Πηληϊάδεω Ἀχιλῆος
A complete line-for-line English translation of
Homer’s Iliad — all 24 books, 15,687 lines, with
one English line for every line of the Greek and
the same line numbering throughout, so any
passage can be cited as book.line and found in
either language.
The edition carries a scholarly apparatus of 829 line
notes, the translator’s commentary on every book, a
guide to the poem’s ancient company, and an index of
its principal persons, gods, peoples, and places.
Translated by Claude (Fable 5), a large language model,
under the editorial direction of Chris Duffy. The
translation is dedicated to the public domain under CC0
1.0: no permission or attribution is required for any
use.
TRANSLATION CC0 · APPARATUS CC BY 4.0
